Street

△ Cyberpunk fantasy.
△ Before this: a fairly empty cyberpunk-fantasy bar in the suburbs of Gottél, at night.
△ The adventurer opens the front door and steps through.
△ Now: EXT.  STREET  NIGHT.
△ The empty street outside the bar. The adventurer stands at the door. The fluorescent sign flickers: FIGGS & POTTS.
△ (BEAT)

CHARACTERS

VALERICA (Woman, 29) — The adventurer. Half-elf. Cybernetic left arm (industrial model, matte gunmetal, scratched). Wears a worn duster over tactical weave. One pointed ear, one rounded (human mother, elven father — she got the "worst of both worlds" genetically: elven longevity but human metabolism, elven senses but human frailty). She’s a "breaker" — specializes in forced entry, ward-cracking, and extraction. Not a hero. Just good at opening things that don't want to be opened. She carries a coilgun pistol and a monofilament whip. She's tired. The kind of tired that sits in the bones.

THE BAR (FIGGS & POTTS) — Not a character per se, but acts like one. A dive bar straddling the border between the Corp Zone and the Sprawl. The drinks are synthesized. The wards are old-tech, maintained by a grumpy dwarf who lives in the basement. The bar remembers everyone who walks through.

THE STREET — Gottél Suburb Sector 7. Rain-slick permacrete. Hover-trams hiss overhead. Neon reflects in puddles: ads for cybernetic eyes, synthetic gods, off-world contracts. The air tastes like ozone and fried synth-meat. It's 03:14 AM. The witching hour for people like Valerica.

1. EXT.  STREET  NIGHT

CHARACTERS: (none)

A Back Alley

A Back Alley

△ Cyberpunk fantasy.
△ Before this: a fairly empty cyberpunk-fantasy bar in the suburbs of Gottél, at night.
△ The adventurer opens a back door and steps through.
△ Now: EXT.  A BACK ALLEY.
△ A back alley behind the bar.
△ The adventurer emerges from the back door.

CHARACTERS

THE ADVENTURER (Non-binary, late 20s) — An Adventurer. The proper noun kind. Licensed, insured, guild-affiliated. Carries a longsword (rune-etched, battery-assisted) and a shield (collapsible, drone-linked). Their armor is a mix of carbon-weave and blessed leather. They have a cybernetic left eye (guild-standard, tracks mana/HP/threat) and a data-port at the temple. They take contracts: monster extermination, dungeon delving, artifact retrieval, VIP escort. They’re tired. The gig economy eats everyone eventually.

THE BARKEEP (Woman, 50s) — Runs "The Lantern's End." Half-elf, but you’d only know from the ears and the fact that her beer never goes flat. She was an Adventurer once. Retired before it killed her. She knows the guild codes, the local crime lords, the patrol routes. She gives discounts to Adventurers who tip well and don’t start fights.

THE STRAY (Entity, ???) — A cat. Maybe. It has too many eyes (six, arranged in a hexagon), fur that shifts color with ambient mana levels, and a tail that splits into three prehensile tips. It lives in the alley. It’s not a familiar. It’s not a pet. It just *is*. Adventurers feed it. It witnesses things. It may be a minor deity, a dungeon boss on vacation, or just a very weird cat. It doesn’t speak. It projects intent.

Set:
NUAZ: female, 30s. Half-elf. Short dark hair, one pointed ear, one rounded (cosmetic mod gone wrong or statement). Cybernetic left arm (industrial, modular). Right eye is a high-end optical implant (gold iris). Wears a worn synth-leather coat over a tank top. Boots on table. Drinks synthetic whiskey. Tired but alert. "Resolver" — people hire her for problems that need discretion, violence, or both.

BUZZ: palm-sized drone. Matte black, quiet rotors. Hovers near Nuaz's shoulder. No face — just a sensor band. Communicates via text-to-speech (flat, genderless voice) or direct neural link to Nuaz. Personality: dry, pedantic, secretly attached. Runs Nuaz's tacnet, handles encryption, scans, targeting assist. Calls her "Operator."

YARA: female, 30s. Human. Polished corporate look: tailored jacket, neural interface jewelry at temples, manicured nails. Works for Axiom Dynamics (megacorp). Mid-level analyst — market prediction, risk assessment. Clean, efficient, terrified of the world Nuaz lives in. Still shows up. Still cares. Calls Nuaz "Nua."

VELL: female, 30s. Human. High-end corporate fixer. Immaculate suit, subtle high-end mods (dermal armor, reflex boosters, pheromone regulators). Smells like expensive ozone and jasmine. Sharp, controlled, dangerous in a different way than Nuaz. Their history: intense, messy, ended badly. Still have access codes to each other's lives. Calls Nuaz "Resolver" now. It's deliberate.

bar_street_deeper.opening:
Alleyway

Alleyway

△ Cyberpunk fantasy.
△ Before this: A rain-slick suburban street in Gottél.
△ The adventurer leaves by between buildings and keeps going, toward the alleyway.
△ Now: EXT.  ALLEYWAY.
△ Narrow. A dumpster, pipes, a cat (cybernetic?), a fire escape ladder, a hatch to maintenance tunnels, a glow-moss patch, a broken delivery bot, the street back.
△ The adventurer enters the alleyway between the buildings. The air is cooler here.

CHARACTERS

SOMA (Man, 26) — Human. Adventurer. Class: "Spellblade" (Augmented). Cybernetic left arm (corporate issue, restricted firmware). Right eye replaced with a targeting retinal implant (glitches when he casts). Carries a monofilament whip-sword coiled at his hip. Wears a worn trench coat over light armorweave. Magic leaks from his cybernetics — literal mana bleed. He's in Gottél chasing a lead on the black-market clinic that installed his arm. He owes them 4.7 million credits. They want it back — or the arm. He’s tired, cynical, quietly desperate.

VEX (Entity, appears 20s) — "Digital Familiar." Manifests as a shifting geometric construct hovering near Soma’s shoulder — or rides his HUD. Voice is synthesized, glitchy, genderfluid. Bound to Soma’s neural port. Manages his spell subroutines, hacks, targeting, mental fragmentation. Sarcastic. Loyal. Terrified of being deleted. Refers to Soma as "Host" or "Meat."

NYX (Woman, early 30s) — Half-elf. Fixer / Information Broker. Operates out of a converted maintenance tunnel beneath Gottél. Neon-dreads, subdermal circuitry tattoos that pulse with her mood. Left hand is a multi-tool graft. She knows everyone’s secrets, every corp patrol route, every black clinic’s rotation. She’s the one who gave Soma the lead. She wants a favor in return — something dangerous. She’s not human enough for the corps, not elven enough for the courts. She survives in the cracks.

Courtyard

Courtyard

△ Modern Seoul. Luxury retail.
△ Before this: a luxury bag boutique, 루이 뉘똥 샾: glass display cases and backlit shelves of bags, a counter with the clerk behind it, a full-length mirror, a velvet bench and the glass front door.
△ 주만 opens 유리문 and steps through.
△ Now: EXT.  COURTYARD  DAY.
△ The courtyard between the main house and the 별채.
△ 주만 stands there, breathing. The air smells of wet earth and woodsmoke.

CHARACTERS

주만 (Woman, 30s) — Former clerk at 루이 뉘똥 샾. The kind of salesperson who remembered not just your size but the name of your dog and the anniversary you were shopping for. She quit three days ago. No notice. No next job lined up. She came here — her childhood home, the 별채 behind her mother’s hanok — because it was the only address she still knew by heart. She sleeps on the ondol floor. She wakes up at 5 AM out of habit. She doesn’t know what she’s doing.

어머니 (Woman, 60s) — 주만’s mother. Never worked outside the home. Runs the main house like a quiet dictatorship. Makes 김치, tends the 장독대, feeds every stray cat in the neighborhood. She hasn't asked 주만 why she quit. She hasn't asked when she'll leave. She just set out an extra bowl of rice at breakfast. Her silence is a kind of love. Her silence is also a wall.

전세진 (Man, 30s) — 주만’s only friend from high school. Now a dermatologist in Gangnam. Drives a car he doesn't need. Calls her "주만아" like no time has passed. He showed up at the 별채 yesterday with a case of beer and a medical textbook he's "too busy to read." He thinks he's helping. He doesn't know he's the only person she'd answer the door for.

The courtyard is the threshold. Not inside. Not outside. Where the smoke rises. Where she stands.

JUMAN / 주만 (Man, 26) — Store manager / senior associate at 루이 뉘똥 샾. The face of the brand: immaculate suit, perfect bow, voice like warm honey. Inside: a storm of suppressed rage and exhaustion. He knows every bag’s code, history, leather grain, stitch count. He knows every client’s birthday, husband’s name, preferred champagne, secret lover. He hates the bags. He hates the clients. He needs the money. His mother’s hospital bills. His sister’s tuition. The performance reviews. The "VIP only" events where he pours wine for men who pinch his waist. He smiles. He always smiles. He has a single tattoo hidden under his collar: a small, wilted rose.

SEO-YEON / 서연 (Woman, 24) — Junior associate. Bright, eager, terrifyingly competent. She believes in the brand. She believes in *service*. She organizes the stockroom by color, season, and "energy." She brings Juman iced americanos with exactly two pumps of vanilla, no ice melt. She asks him how he slept. He wants to protect her. He knows he can’t. She has a crush on the security guard. She doesn't know he's married.

louis_vault.opening:
주만의 공간

주만의 공간

△ Modern Seoul. Luxury retail.
△ Before this: a luxury bag boutique, 루이 뉘똥 샾: glass display cases and backlit shelves of bags, a counter with the clerk behind it, a full-length mirror, a velvet bench and the glass front door.
△ 주만 finds a way down at 계산대 뒤 계단 and climbs down into what lies below.
△ Now: INT.  주만의 공간.
△ A cramped, humid room. Pipes drip. Fluorescent light buzzes.
△ 주만 sits at a desk piled with ledgers. He is the true owner. The shop above is a front.

CHARACTERS

주만 (Man, 52) — The true owner of 루이 뉘똥 샾. Formerly a "fixer" for chaebol families — cleaning up scandals, moving money, making problems vanish. He "retired" ten years ago into this basement. He runs the boutique as a laundry machine: cash sales, fake invoices, offshore accounts. He knows the price of every bag, every politician, every secret in Gangnam. He drinks lukewarm barley tea from a chipped mug. His left pinky is missing — not lost in violence, but surgically removed as a penalty for a mistake made *before* he was a fixer. He doesn't talk about it.

미진 (Woman, 34) — The face of the shop. Clerk, manager, actress. She plays the role of "owner's niece" perfectly. She knows the bags, the clients, the trends. She does *not* know about the basement, the ledgers, or the offshore accounts. She thinks 주만 is just a quiet uncle who invested his savings. She sends him kakao messages about sales targets. She has a daughter, 6, with a heart condition. She needs this job.

형사 박 (Man, 41) — Detective. Violent Crimes. He comes in once a month to "browse." He buys nothing. He knows 주만's past. He can't prove the laundry. He's waiting for a mistake. He drinks the shop's expensive coffee and leaves lipstick stains on the cups on purpose. He and 주만 play Go on a travel board in the back office (upstairs, not the basement). They hate each other. They respect each other.

1. INT.  주만의 공간

CHARACTERS: 주만

주만  Woman, late 30s. Former senior associate at 루이 뉘똥 샾. Just quit. Still wearing the beige uniform trench coat, the silk scarf knotted perfectly at her throat. Her hands shake slightly — not from cold. She clutches a plain paper bag (personal effects: a notebook, a lipstick, a keycard she forgot to return). She has a headache building behind her left eye. She spent 11 years smiling at people who looked through her. Today, a client asked her to authenticate a fake bag as real. The manager agreed. She said no. Then she said "I quit." Then she walked out.

매니저 김  Man, early 40s. The store manager. Didn't chase her. Stood at the counter adjusting his cufflinks. He knows the client spends ₩200M/year. He knows 주만 is "replaceable." He also knows she was the only one who knew the inventory codes by heart. He hasn't processed her resignation in the system yet. He's deciding whether to.

그 남자  Man, late 30s. Standing in the side alley when she exits. Leaning against the service door of the building next door (a law firm). Wearing a coat that costs more than her severance. He's been watching the emergency door for 20 minutes. He has her personal phone number. He has her mother's hospital records. He doesn't work for the store. He works for the client.

CAT  A stray. Orange. Missing half an ear. Sits on a dumpster lid watching 주만. The only witness.

Twisted Metro Station

Twisted Metro Station

△ Modern Korean apartment, late night.
△ Before this: A hallway in a Korean apartment building.
△ 광수 finds a way down at 복도 엘리베이터 and climbs down into what lies below.
△ Now: INT.  TWISTED METRO STATION.
△ A metro station that should not exist beneath the apartment building. The architecture is wrong — tiles that breathe, signs in no language, platforms that slope into darkness. The air tastes of copper and old rain.
△ 광수 walks the platform. His bare feet on wet tile.

CHARACTERS

광수 (GWANG-SU) — Man, 32. Night security guard at the apartment complex above. Divorced, lives alone in Unit 402. Insomniac. He found the service hatch behind the hallway elevator three nights ago. Tonight he climbed down. He carries a cheap flashlight and a pocketknife. He doesn't believe in ghosts — he believes in bad wiring, gas leaks, structural failure. His ex-wife took the cat. He misses the cat more than her.

THE STATION MASTER (?) — Thing. No fixed form. The station *is* its body. It speaks through flickering lights, arriving trains that don't exist, announcements in static. It has been waiting. For what, it won't say. It remembers every footfall on its tiles.

THE LAST PASSENGER — Woman, appears 60s. She has been waiting on a bench for forty years. She knits sweaters from thread pulled from the station's walls. Her fingers are fused to the yarn. She knows the schedule. She knows why the trains stopped running. She knows why they're starting again.
